title: Complete Modified Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for one-dimensional quantum Spin Chain
authors: Li Gao, Jingyu Guo, Sihao Wang
abstract: We prove a complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality with a system-size-independent constant for Chen--Kastoryano--Gilyén Gibbs samplers on one-dimensional spin chain at every fixed positive temperature. The result holds for Hamiltonians with bounded finite-range interactions, including noncommuting and spatially nonuniform interactions. It yields trace and diamond mixing times of order $O(\log N+\log(1/ε))$. The proof establishes complete spatial entropy factorization and absorbs quasi-local errors as conditional relative entropy at the original joint state and reference. The static estimate also yields a system-size-independent CMLSI for the single-site Petz heat-bath and regularised heat-bath dynamics.
summary: This paper proves a complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for quantum spin chains undergoing Markovian evolution towards equilibrium. By establishing this inequality, the authors derive an optimal, system-size-independent bound for the mixing time in both trace and diamond norms. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for quantifying how quickly quantum systems thermalize.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the convergence rate (mixing time) for preparing quantum Gibbs states using quantum Markov evolution, particularly for systems with complex, non-commuting interactions.
main_result: They establish a complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (CMLSI) with a constant independent of system size, leading to an optimal mixing time bound of $O(\log N + \log(1/\epsilon))$ for both trace and diamond norms.
method: The proof relies on establishing a complete spatial factorization of the relative entropy and bounding the entropy production rate using local estimates derived from the quantum Markov generator.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional quantum spin chain described by a Hamiltonian with finite-range, bounded interactions. The dynamics are governed by the Chen–Kastoryano–Gilyén (CKG) generator, driving the system towards the Gibbs state $\sigma = e^{- eta H} / 	ext{Tr}(e^{- eta H})$.
key_observables: Relative Entropy $D(ho\|\sigma)$, Entropy Production $I_L(ho)$, Trace distance $d_{	ext{Tr}}(t)$, and Diamond distance $d_{\diamond}(t)$.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature $ eta$, interaction range $r_0$, and interaction strength $J_0$. The results are shown to be independent of system size $N$.
main_assumptions: The result holds for open chains and cycles with uniformly bounded, finite-range interactions, without assuming commutativity or translation-invariance.
figures_summary: The notes mention Figure 1 illustrates the proof structure: spatial/dynamical inputs lead to complete relative entropy decay, which in turn yields the mixing bounds.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general MLSI results to a *complete* inequality involving an arbitrary reference system $R$, which is the key step yielding the optimal, size-independent mixing time bound.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of mixing times using functional inequalities like MLSI is fundamental for understanding thermalization and equilibration in complex quantum many-body systems, directly impacting how we model physical processes like quantum thermalization.
